indication: Adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma that progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody (accelerated approval)
headline: The FDA granted accelerated approval to RYBREVANT FASPRO on November 5, 2026 as a single agent for adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after platinum-based chemotherapy and an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody.
pdufa_note: The FDA's accelerated approval letter for BLA 761433 supplement 2, signed November 5, 2026 (FDA letter), covers RYBREVANT FASPRO as a single agent for adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody. The letter states that it is not indicated for HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, and that the supplemental application was received on May 20, 2026. Johnson & Johnson announced the approval the same evening and reported a 42 percent overall response rate (95 percent confidence interval, 32 to 52 percent) (Johnson & Johnson, November 5, 2026). We hold no publicly disclosed PDUFA goal date for this supplement, so no early or late margin is given.
h1: RYBREVANT FASPRO FDA approval for head and neck cancer: Nov 5, 2026

indication: Adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer ineligible for or refusing cisplatin-based chemotherapy, with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv before cystectomy, then alone after it
headline: Imfinzi (durvalumab) was approved in the US on November 13, 2026 with neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin-ejfv, then as adjuvant monotherapy after radical cystectomy, for cisplatin-ineligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
pdufa_note: Drugs@FDA records BLA 761069 supplement 59 (efficacy) for Imfinzi as approved on November 13, 2026 (Drugs@FDA). AstraZeneca announced that evening that Imfinzi in combination with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv as neoadjuvant treatment, followed by Imfinzi monotherapy as adjuvant treatment after radical cystectomy, was approved for adults with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who are ineligible for or have refused cisplatin-based chemotherapy (AstraZeneca, November 13, 2026). We hold no publicly disclosed PDUFA goal date for this supplement, so no early or late margin is given.
h1: Imfinzi (durvalumab) FDA approval for muscle-invasive bladder cancer: Nov 13, 2026

indication: Adults with polymyalgia rheumatica with an inadequate response to corticosteroids or who cannot tolerate a corticosteroid taper
headline: The FDA approved COSENTYX (secukinumab) on November 16, 2026 for adults with polymyalgia rheumatica, a new indication.
pdufa_note: The FDA's supplement approval letter for BLA 125504 supplement 101, signed November 16, 2026 (FDA letter), adds a new indication for the treatment of adult patients with polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR); the letter states that the supplemental application was received on January 16, 2026. openFDA's Drugs@FDA data lists the approval under November 17; the date here is the letter's own signature date. Novartis announced the approval that evening (US Eastern time; its release is datelined Basel, November 17) for Cosentyx 150 mg in adults with PMR who have had an inadequate response to corticosteroids or who cannot tolerate a corticosteroid taper (Novartis, November 17, 2026). We hold no publicly disclosed PDUFA goal date for this supplement, so no early or late margin is given.
h1: COSENTYX (secukinumab) FDA approval for polymyalgia rheumatica: Nov 16, 2026
